record.paper_title: Open problems on billiards and geometric optics
record.context_brief: Integrable shapes for the modified billiard map
record.original_question: For the same symplectic map T associated with a closed smooth strictly convex plane curve γ, determine which shapes of γ, other than circles, make T integrable.

evidence.quote: Question 2: What are the shapes of γ (other than the circles) such that T is an integrable map?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let γ be a closed smooth strictly convex plane curve, and let T: γ × γ → γ × γ be the symplectic billiard map associated with γ, defined as follows. Given an ordered pair of distinct points (x, y) on γ, define T(x, y) = (y, z), where z ∈ γ is uniquely determined by the condition that the tangent line to γ at y is parallel to the chord xz. The map T preserves the symplectic 2-form ω on γ × γ (away from the diagonal) given by ω = d x ∧ d y, with respect to which it is a monotone twist map.

The map T is called integrable if there exists a continuous, non-constant function F: γ × γ → ℝ that is invariant under T (equivalently, a foliation of an open subset of phase space by smooth invariant curves on which T acts as a rotation, i.e., a caustic foliation). It is known that when γ is a circle, T is integrable (concentric circles serve as caustics), and by affine equivariance the same holds when γ is any ellipse.

Determine all shapes of γ, other than circles, for which the symplectic map T is integrable.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is an analogue of the Birkhoff conjecture for symplectic billiards. Ellipses are known to give integrable maps by affine equivariance. A recent result of Bialy and Tsodikovich ("Totally integrable symplectic billiards are ellipses", arXiv:2305.19701, published in Advances in Mathematics, 2024) proves that under the stronger assumption of total integrability of the symplectic billiard map on a strictly convex curve with everywhere positive curvature, γ must be an ellipse. Related rigidity results (Bialy–Mironov type, centrally symmetric case) appear in arXiv:2402.19154. The full classification (without the total integrability assumption, only local/near-boundary integrability) remains open.

status_evidence.title: Totally integrable symplectic billiards are ellipses
status_evidence.snippet: A totally integrable strictly-convex symplectic billiard table, whose boundary has everywhere strictly positive curvature, must be an ellipse.
status_evidence.claim: Settles the symplectic-billiard Birkhoff-type question under total integrability, giving a partial answer (ellipses).

status_evidence.title: Bialy–Mironov type rigidity for centrally symmetric symplectic billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Rigidity result for centrally symmetric symplectic billiards in the spirit of Bialy–Mironov.
status_evidence.claim: Further partial rigidity progress on the integrability question for symplectic billiards.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry (2026)
status_evidence.snippet: Subsequent 2025 workshop problem list continues to discuss integrability problems for billiard-type symplectic maps.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates the general classification problem is still of active interest.
